- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or apply mean-reversion bias toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; anchor forecast to 14-day moving average of price + sentiment-weighted adjustment (e.g., +0.5x sentiment if >0.67, -0.5x if <0.33).
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean-reversion correction toward 30-day rolling average of past 10–15 days.
